# rc2 selected-session conversation hot installation

This independent regression uses the official rc2 mac-arm64 application and the
actual final candidate archive. It preserves PR72's frozen original rc1 failure
baseline. Its isolated environment, ASAR identity checks, public session APIs,
model veto, natural-exit observer and diagnostic projection are adapted from the
reviewed PR68/PR72 fixtures into this directory; those files are not modified.

Stock creates one blank standard session, refreshes the public catalog, opens
it once and verifies its real current adapter id and mainView retain. Installation
then uses the real plugin-manager file-bundle transaction. The test requires an
`applied` receipt and identical Electron/Host PIDs; restart-required cannot pass.
It never reopens the session after installation. The selected identity and
blank/prompt flags must remain correct while the actual renderer converges to
the current Host graph. Installed client bytes are checked against the frozen
archive; the Host rows must resolve callbacks from that installed package.

Renderer errors and synchronous public slot-error/abdication events remain
failures. Strict conversation visibility, original provider state, unique model
and native label occupancy, unchanged label owner, native QueueDock registration
and a visible composer are required. A natural Electron/Host shutdown must
reach disposed/before-exit/exit with exit 0 and no signal/model call. Cleanup
failure cannot turn the test green. No prompt, account, credential file, model
API or computer-use action is used. The native OS home/log exception is restricted
to the disposable hosted runner and does not permit reading account data.

Full evidence stays in the artifact. Bounded `OMD_HOT_DIAG ` log summaries retain
only enumerated states and numeric identities, excluding error text, paths,
settings, environment, session content and receipt details. The Linux lifecycle
tests execute actual transpiled apply/service/QueueDock source and Cordis 4.0.5
with synthetic SlotRegistry/UI/session collaborators. They establish the ordering
barrier and cleanup, not a real selected-session renderer result. Only the
separate macOS CI job can establish that result.
